scope: answer whether we reuse the 2697 server binary and whether we can build our own instrumented server

current_server.what_runs: runs/2697-server-test/codol_dedrun.exe (a patched copy, enterworld12), started from cmd-28970.json
current_server.kind: the real 2697 dedicated server binary, not a UI shell; it binds TCP/UDP 28970, runs mp_cross_fire with 11 bots and logs CoDOL lines

source_available.build_system: top-level GNU makefile; also mbedtls CMakeLists and tomcrypt makefile under src/

toolchain.consequence: the source cannot be built on this machine as-is; a MinGW-w64/MSYS2 or MSVC toolchain must be installed first, along with the crypto dependencies the makefile expects

why_building_our_own_server_is_the_right: we are currently blind-patching a stripped binary and guessing at client_t offsets and address comparisons
with a built server we can print exactly what SV_PacketEvent receives, what NET_CompareAdr returns, and how client_t fields change per packet
the remoteAddress=0.0.0.0 problem could be fixed directly in source instead of rewriting memory each session
we can add observation endpoints (console command or a small admin channel) that dump client state on demand

options.option: A. install MinGW-w64/MSYS2 + make, build the 2697 source with instrumentation
options.cost: toolchain setup plus dependency resolution; unknown but bounded

options.option: B. continue binary patching and memory reads
options.benefit: slower and error-prone; every hypothesis costs a full session

recommendation: try A: install a toolchain, build the unmodified source first to confirm it compiles, then add logging and rebuild. Keep B as fallback while the build is being set up.
next: check whether a MinGW-w64 or MSVC toolchain can be installed in this environment
if yes, attempt an unmodified build of runs/2697-native-src and see which dependencies fail
meanwhile continue the early remoteAddress.ip rewrite experiment (client_t was not yet present 4 s after start-challenge)
